aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer was defined as stage T4, N1, or M1 or prostate cancer mortality. Advanced restricted prostate cancer excluded men with missing stage and men with localized prostate cancer who died of prostate cancer. High-grade prostate cancer was defined as Gleason score at least 8 or poorly differentiated/undifferentiated disease.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: The primary outcome measures were advanced (stage T4, N1, or M1 or PC mortality), advanced restricted (excluded men with missing stage and those with localized PC who died of PC), and high-grade PC (Gleason score ≥8 or poorly differentiated/undifferentiated) and PC mortality.
study_design: Pooled analysis of primary data from 15 prospective cohorts using Cox proportional hazards regression and random-effects pooling.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: There were 842 149 men followed for up to 9 to 22 years between 1985 and 2009 across studies.
reason: The pooled prospective cohort analysis explicitly evaluated incident advanced, advanced restricted, and high-grade prostate cancer, as well as prostate cancer mortality. Localized and low/intermediate-grade endpoints were also reported, but the abstract did not report an overall or total incident prostate cancer association.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Intake of dietary fiber overall, from fruits, and from vegetables was not associated with risk of advanced (n = 4863), advanced restricted (n = 2978), or high-grade PC (n = 9673) or PC mortality (n = 3097).
estimate_classifications.reason: The row specifically represents the highest-versus-lowest quintile association between total dietary fiber and advanced prostate cancer, an explicitly aggressive incident endpoint. Its numerical estimate comes from supplied full-text evidence, while the endpoint and exposure association are established by the abstract.
